- Register: "Zhonghang Electronicc Measuring Instruments (Xi'an) Co., Ltd."
- Document: "Zhonghang Electronic Measuring Instruments (Xi'an) Co., Ltd."

The register has "Electronicc" (double c) while the document has "Electronic" (correct spelling). "Electronicc" appears to be a typo/OCR noise — an extra "c". The rules say spelling drift = same-entity. Extraction artifacts/OCR noise = document-noise with best_value from the register. But here the OCR noise is in the register value? The register likely was extracted from the certificate too. Which value should the fused record carry?

Rules: "spelling drift, legal-suffix drift, accent differences = same-entity." So verdict = same-entity. Best value: the correct spelling "Zhonghang Electronic Measuring Instruments (Xi'an) Co., Ltd." — the document's value, since the certificate is the legal instrument and the register's "Electronicc" is a typo. The rule "document-noise with best_value from the register" applies when extraction artifacts are in the document. Here the drift seems to be in the register ("Electronicc" is clearly the typo). Since same-entity, best value should be the correct spelling, which is the document's form. Given the certificate is the legal instrument and the document spelling is correct English, best_value = document value.

So: verdict "same-entity", best_value "Zhonghang Electronic Measuring Instruments (Xi'an) Co., Ltd.", why: single-character spelling drift ("Electronicc" vs "Electronic"), same company; document form is the correct spelling from the legal instrument.
